# vectordata fixture

This directory is a vectordata catalog (`catalog.json`) naming one dataset, `polydat-tiny`, whose `tiny/dataset.yaml` declares a `default` profile of six base vectors and three query vectors of dimension 3 (`base_vectors.fvec`, `query_vectors.fvec`: each record a little-endian `i32` dimension and that many little-endian `f32` values), a `u8` metadata facet with one value per base vector (`metadata_content.u8`: 2, 0, 2, 5, 2, 0), and an `i32` predicates facet with one value per query (`metadata_predicates.i32`: 2, 5, 2). The ground truth of each query is in the same record layout: its two nearest base vectors (`neighbor_indices.ivec`: 0 1, 1 0, 1 2) and their squared Euclidean distances (`neighbor_distances.fvec`), and its nearest base vector among those whose metadata value is the query's predicate (`prefiltered_neighbor_indices.ivec`: 0, 3, 2, which polydat reads as the `filtered_neighbor_indices` facet) with its distance (`prefiltered_neighbor_distances.fvec`). The metadata results (`metadata_results.ivvec`) are variable-length records, one per query, naming every base vector whose metadata value is the query's predicate (0 2 4, 3, 0 2 4). The two YAML/JSON files are written by hand; the nine binary facets, 6 to 96 bytes each, are the output of `facet_files` in `tests/vectordata_fixture.rs`, written by its ignored `write_the_fixture` test (`cargo nextest run -p polydat --features vectordata --run-ignored only -E 'test(write_the_fixture)'`) and held to that generator by `the_fixture_is_what_its_generator_writes`; `the_ground_truth_is_the_true_nearest_neighbors` holds the ground truth and the metadata results to a brute-force search over the vectors. Each test process copies this directory under the target's scratch space and reaches the dataset by name through a `catalogs.yaml` it writes under `$VECTORDATA_HOME`, so every read goes through the catalog, `dataset.yaml`, and the vectordata readers, and the offset index the variable-length reader writes beside `metadata_results.ivvec` lands in the copy.
